title: Web Development Zurich: Multilingual Websites | 22 Signals
description: Web development for Zurich companies: multilingual websites and client portals built for German, French, Italian and English, accessible to WCAG by default.
h1: Web development for Zurich companies that sell in more than one language
intro: We build websites, client portals and e-commerce for Zurich companies that need to work in German, French, Italian and English without four separate sites to maintain. Every build is accessible to WCAG standards by default, set up properly for search in each language and planned around the revised FADP. You get a written scope within 5 to 7 days and launch dates in writing.

sections.h: The multilingual problem most Swiss sites get wrong
p: A Zurich company selling across Switzerland usually needs at least German and French, often Italian, and English for international clients and staff. Many sites handle this badly. Language versions drift apart, some pages exist in one language only, the language switcher drops visitors on the home page, and search engines index the wrong version for the wrong audience.

Good web development solves this in the structure, not with patches. Each language gets its own clean URLs, pages are linked to their equivalents, search engines are told which version serves which audience, and editors can see at a glance which translations are missing or out of date.

p: Every site we build follows WCAG accessibility guidelines as standard. That means proper headings, readable contrast, full keyboard use, clear form errors, captions and text alternatives. It is the right thing to do, and it helps search engines and AI assistants read your pages too.

There is also a commercial reason in Switzerland. Swiss public bodies already work to accessibility standards based on WCAG, and many large companies ask suppliers for the same. Swiss firms that sell certain products and services to consumers in the EU now also face the European Accessibility Act. Building it in from the start costs far less than fixing it later.

sections.h: Built to the standard Zurich clients expect
p: Swiss buyers notice details. A misaligned table, a broken link in the French version or a contact form that rejects a Swiss postcode tells a prospective client something about how you work. We test every template in every language, on real devices and screen readers, before launch.

Security gets the same attention. Client portals use strong authentication, role-based access and encrypted storage, and we document how data moves so your data protection officer can review it. For financial firms, we keep marketing pages and client areas separate so content changes never touch sensitive systems.

Talk is a 15-minute call about what the site must achieve and who uses it. Plan is discovery: we review your current site, analytics and search data, agree the language and page structure and deliver a written scope within 5 to 7 days. Build covers design, development, content migration and testing, with each milestone dated in writing. Grow means monitoring speed, search and enquiries after launch and improving what the data shows.
We deliver in English. Copy in German, French or Italian comes from your team, your translators or localisation partners we arrange, and we load and check every version.

faqs.q: What does web development Zurich firms commission usually include?
faqs.a: Discovery, information architecture, design, development, content migration, testing in every language, accessibility checks, search setup and launch. Many projects add a client portal or e-commerce, plus ongoing support after go-live.

faqs.q: Do you write the German and French content?
faqs.a: No. We deliver in English and do not claim in-house German or French copywriters. Translations come from your team, your translators or localisation partners we arrange. We build the structure, load each version and check layouts, forms and search settings in every language.

faqs.q: Should we have one site or one per language?
faqs.a: Almost always one site with language versions. That keeps design, code and content in one place, makes it easy to see missing translations and lets search engines understand which version is for which audience. Separate domains only make sense in a few special cases.

Yes, on every build. We follow WCAG guidelines as standard and test with keyboards and screen readers. If you sell to EU consumers, we also check the parts of the European Accessibility Act that apply to your site.

faqs.q: Can you host the site in Switzerland?
faqs.a: Yes, where it makes sense. Marketing sites usually run well on a global content delivery network, while portals holding client data can be hosted in Swiss cloud regions. We recommend based on what data the site holds and what your clients expect.

faqs.q: Which content management systems do you use?
faqs.a: We choose based on your team and needs, from WordPress and headless systems to custom builds for portals. The deciding factors are how many languages you manage, who edits content and which systems the site must connect to.
